title: Air Force UFO files: what remains after declassification
excerpt: Military reports on UFOs in Spain were kept classified for decades at the Air Force Headquarters. What remains in the archives after declassification and what is still unexplained.
content:
For decades, the Air Force reports on unidentified objects in Spanish skies were classified material, kept at the Air Force Headquarters. The subject comes from a Milenio 3 (Cadena SER) special broadcast in 2008, and at foro3d.com we have reviewed how the declassification process unfolded. What remains in the archives?

From classified to nearly 2,000 consultable pages 📄

In 1976 part of it came to light when a senior officer handed documents to journalist J. J. Benítez, who published them in a book the following year. The major opening came in 1992: the Air Operational Command began reviewing the files and, between 1992 and the late nineties, 83 files with 122 cases and nearly 2,000 pages were declassified, available for consultation in the library of the Air Force Headquarters. Many came with explanations such as weather balloons, planets or aircraft; others remain unresolved.

The mystery that fits in an archive record 🗂️

The declassification sparked a long controversy among researchers over whether everything had been handed over. And there the doubt remains, comfortable in its folder: if every weather balloon and every misidentified planet has its record, how many records are still to appear? If you know any detail of the process or have consulted those files, tell us: your contribution can help other readers.
